newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Seven die in Australian cliff collapse - police.
newsitem.headline: Seven die in Australian cliff collapse - police.

text.p: Seven people died on Friday when a cliff collapsed on a school group walking along a beach in Western Australia, police said.

Acting superintendent Bill Rowtcliff told Australian Broadcasting Corp television he did not know whether others in the group were still trapped in the rockfall or had been rescued. It was not immediately clear how many children and adults were involved.
"Unfortunately, we have seven deceased people. I don't know if they were children, or adults who were with them, or some of each," Rowtcliff said.
The accident happened at about three p.m. (0700 GMT) near the Cowaramup National Park about 200 km (120 miles) southwest of the Western Australia capital of Perth.
Rowtcliff said the group were walking along the beach when an overhanging ledge collapsed on them.
Another policeman from nearby Margaret River said the group had just finished a surfing lesson. Cowaramup Bay is a popular surfing site on Australia Indian Ocean coast.
